name: Museum of Antioquia
scope: Standing former municipal palace used by the Museum of Antioquia in Medellín, including the Carabobo entrance, present exterior and open courtyard elevations.
era: Standing 1930s municipal palace after the conversion to the Museum of Antioquia in 2000.

originalReview.notes: The creator-dedicated location plan identifies the former municipal palace facing Plaza Botero, with two parallel main courts, a central cross-range and narrow secondary rear lightwells. Courtyard proportions are approximate.
The north court has pale piers, open upper galleries, a gray sill course and octagonal central fountain surrounded by planting. Only built fabric and fountain shape inform the reconstruction.
The rear court has pale gray masonry bands, deeply set rectangular openings and a shallow rectangular pool. Temporary café furnishings are omitted.

review.method: Exact Qualla location diagram and verified photographer-dedicated courtyard originals
review.notes: Started with the exact published Qualla map. The attribution-conditioned hero and plaque photographs were excluded. Used two photographer-dedicated original Commons photographs for courtyard architecture only. The city-block outline is native mapped geometry. The conservation report describes the main elevation in writing.
